title: Proper direct-image constructibility over a Noetherian base
statement: Fix universes u and u+1, a prime ell, a field k in universe u with ringChar(k) different from ell, schemes Z,Y in universe u, a morphism aY:Y→Spec(k), a Noetherian Y, and a proper p:Z→Y. Let Λ be a commutative condensed ring object, with its specified multiplication, having IsEllAdicFinitenessCoefficient ell Λ: a finite normed Q_ell extension, the induced ring of integers of a finite embedded extension, the finite-subextension-valued algebraic closure, or the closed unit ball of a finite normed extension. Put Λ_T=p_T^*Λ and D_T=D(Mod(Λ_T)), with the actual total right derived functor Rp_* [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Constructibility means stratified local finite presentation [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. The coefficient certification is the four-constructor class in WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.RingObjects.Condensed.FinitenessCoefficient, with its monoid-object index, rather than a new coefficient construction. For every bounded K in D_Z whose cohomology module objects are constructible, and every integer q, H^q(Rp_*K) is a constructible Λ_Y-module object. This assertion imposes no upper bound on the cohomology of Rp_*K. No finite-type or separatedness assumption is imposed on aY, and k may have characteristic zero.

source.place: Integral and rational proper finiteness, constructibility clauses; Bhatt--Scholze 6.7.2 and Remark 6.8.15.

proof.text: For an integral coefficient ring, reduce a constructible heart object modulo powers of a uniformizer. Proper torsion finiteness makes the derived images constructible, and proper base change identifies the reductions. Integral direct image preserves derived completeness. The adic constructibility criterion identifies the resulting complex as constructible; on a Noetherian target its cohomology has a finite stratification by finitely presented local models. This is Bhatt--Scholze 6.7.1--6.7.2 combined with 6.6.11.

For finite rational coefficients choose integral lattices on a finite stratification. Inverting ell commutes with proper direct image by bounded-below qcqs continuity. Finite gluing and localization preserve constructibility. For the condensed algebraic closure use finite coefficient descent of the finitely many local presentations and scalar extension along the filtered system of finite fields. This is the coefficient passage of Bhatt--Scholze 6.8.11--6.8.15. To compare an abstract finite normed extension E with the embedded presentation, choose a Q_ell-embedding into the algebraic closure; uniqueness of the extended absolute value makes it isometric. It identifies the unit ball with the induced valuation ring, and continuous-function sheaf functoriality transports the coefficient ring and all module-object functors. This covers the explicit unit-ball constructor too.

Constructible module objects form a weak Serre class for these coefficients on a Noetherian scheme. Apply induction on a finite cohomological interval for K, using good-truncation triangles. Derived pushforward is triangulated; the long exact cohomology sequence writes the middle cohomology as an extension of a cokernel by a kernel. These are constructible by the Serre property and the induction hypothesis. Zero complexes, empty strata and all integer degrees are included.

    [MonObj Λ] [IsCommMonObj Λ] [IsEllAdicFinitenessCoefficient ℓ Λ]

    (p : Z ⟶ Y) [IsProper p]

      (condensedRingObj Λ Z)))
